description.narrative: IFC, already an investor in Actis Asia Climate Transition (AACT), proposes to invest up to US$20 million (alongside an investment of US$80 million by AACT) through an Actis partnership, which together with other Actis partnerships will indirectly hold, subject to regulatory approvals, a 49% stake in Bharat Grid Private Limited (BGPL). BGPL is an Indian smart meter platform established by the EDF group which will bid for, own, and operate 10-year smart meter concessions under the Indian government's Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) including other smart metering projects/schemes in India.

The project is expected to improve the quality of electricity supply in the states of Gujarat and Punjab by financing the roll-out of 7.3 million smart meters that can support the reduction of distribution losses. Also, it is expected that the introduction of smart meters could have positive environmental effects through its enabling of real time monitoring of consumption which reduces the amount of electricity lost during distribution and encourages efficient usage. By so doing, it could lead to energy savings and reduction of GHG emissions. At the market level, the Project is expected to strengthen resilience of electricity systems, supporting smart-grid transition across key states in India, through demonstration and replication effects. By enabling the mainstreaming of Advance Metering Infrastructure (AMI) and ICT systems, the Project will demonstrate an effective rollout of replicable smart-grid solutions that support the Government of Indias RDSS. By so doing, it is expected to deepen Indias smart grid transformation and encourage much needed private investments in smart meters.
